title: Systems and automation in Payson, AZ | Creosote Labs
meta_description: Creosote Labs consolidates spreadsheets and disconnected tools into one system for Payson businesses, and automates repetitive work.
intro: Contractors, clinics, and retail stores in Payson tend to accumulate tools over time. A contractor might track jobs in Excel, invoice from QuickBooks, and schedule crews by text message. A clinic might keep its practice management system, a separate spreadsheet for referrals, and paper intake forms. Systems and automation work applies when the same information lives in several of those places and someone has to keep them in agreement by hand, usually at the end of the day or the end of the month.

Creosote Labs works with Payson and Rim Country businesses to consolidate spreadsheets and disconnected tools into one system of record, build internal tools for scheduling, quoting, tracking, and reporting, and automate data entry, follow-up, and document generation. Every system is documented and handed over to the staff who will run it. Pricing begins with a one-day operations review at $3,000, which produces a written assessment and a quote for each recommendation; implementation is quoted from that review, with no hourly billing.
projects: A job tracker for a general contractor that replaces a shared Excel workbook and pushes completed jobs to QuickBooks for invoicing.
A quoting tool for an HVAC or plumbing company that produces an estimate from a site visit form.
A booking and inventory system for a cabin rental or outfitter that replaces a calendar, a spreadsheet, and a stack of paper waivers.
An automated follow-up sequence for a retail store or service business that sends reminders and review requests after each sale or job.
A reporting dashboard that pulls weekly numbers from QuickBooks and the scheduling system so the owner no longer assembles them by hand.

faqs.q: Does the business have to replace the software it already uses?
faqs.a: Not necessarily; many projects connect the existing tools, such as QuickBooks and a scheduling or practice management system, and replace only the spreadsheets that sit between them. The operations review identifies which pieces to keep.

faqs.q: How is a systems project priced?
faqs.a: It starts with a one-day operations review at $3,000, which produces a written assessment and a quote for each recommendation. Implementation is fixed price from that quote, with no hourly billing, and the review fee is credited toward implementation that begins within 90 days.

faqs.q: What happens to the system after the project ends?
faqs.a: We document it and hand it over to the staff who will use it day to day. The business owns the system and the documentation.
